titulo: Bond Yields Surge and Oil Shocks Shake Global Markets
resumo: Financial markets faced extreme turbulence in October 2026 as **soaring government bond yields** reached multi-decade highs, driven by persistent inflation and resilient economic data. Energy markets experienced severe volatility, with Brent crude nearing **$100 a barrel** and diesel shortages triggering emergency stock releases by the G7. Despite these mounting economic pressures and a sharp slowdown in US job creation, major stock indices managed to reach **new record highs**, heavily supported by artificial intelligence investments. Meanwhile, central banks maintained a cautious stance on interest rates amid ongoing global trade and fiscal concerns.

themes.texto: Long-term government bond yields surged across major economies, with US 10-year Treasury yields hitting their highest levels since 2002. The relentless debt sell-off increased borrowing costs for governments and corporations alike, though strong demand at subsequent auctions provided occasional relief.

Geopolitical conflicts and refining constraints pushed oil prices higher, with Brent crude approaching $100 per barrel. In response to soaring fuel costs and threatened export bans, G7 nations agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency reserves.

Economic data revealed a sharp deceleration in hiring, as the US economy added just 29,000 jobs in September and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. The softer labour figures led traders to scale back expectations for immediate further interest rate hikes.

Technology stocks continued to drive market momentum, with the S&P 500 touching record highs despite broader economic headwinds. Corporations across sectors aggressively pursued AI integration, hardware deals, and specialised agent software despite lingering questions over immediate financial returns.

momentos.facto: US 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2002 while UK long-term bond yields reached 6% for the first time since 1998.
The US jobs report showed the economy added just 29,000 jobs in September and unemployment rose to 4.2%.
G7 nations agreed to a coordinated release of up to 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel stocks to combat surging fuel prices.
The average five-year fixed mortgage rate in the UK hit the 6% barrier for the first time in three years.
The S&P 500 climbed to a record high, boosted by corporate earnings optimism and a rally in artificial intelligence stocks.
Federal Reserve minutes from the September meeting revealed hawkish unity among policymakers regarding ongoing inflation risks.

classes.leitura: Heavy selling pushed long-term yields to multi-decade highs, though late-month auctions found solid investor demand.
Major indices like the S&P 500 reached record highs driven by AI tech strength, while European stocks faced local fiscal pressures.
Brent crude pushed toward $100 per barrel amid refining bottlenecks and Middle East tensions before easing on emergency reserve releases.
The US dollar strengthened on rising yields and European political risks, pushing the euro down to multi-month lows.
